ruleset.name: jpinpoint-nextgen-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint "nextgen" rule set: rewrites of existing rules using newer PMD language-module features (e.g. Kotlin type-resolution XPath functions from PMD 7.28.0). These rules REQUIRE a PMD version that supports those features and therefore are NOT included in the standard jpinpoint-kotlin-rules.xml, to keep that file working on older PMD versions as before. Instead, they are published separately in jpinpoint-kotlin-rules-nextgen.xml, which overlays jpinpoint-kotlin-rules.xml and replaces the listed rules with their improved nextgen version. Use jpinpoint-kotlin-rules-nextgen.xml only if your PMD version supports the features used (see each rule's description for its minimum PMD version).

rule.name: AvoidMultipleConcatStatements
rule.message: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Use StringBuilder append.
rule.description: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Problem: Each statement with one or more +-operators creates a hidden temporary StringBuilder, a char[] and a new String object, which all have to be garbage collected. Solution: Use StringBuilder.append. Nextgen: uses Kotlin type-resolution XPath functions, requires PMD >= 7.28.0. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath
property.value: //FunctionBody[ (: collect, per qualifying concat statement, the name of the String var/property it concatenates to :) let $qualifyingNames := .//Assignment[ .//(AssignmentAndOperator/T-ADD_ASSIGNMENT | AdditiveOperator/T-ADD) (: exclude assignments like map[key + "A"] = ... :) and not((AssignableExpression|DirectlyAssignableExpression)//IndexingSuffix) ] /(AssignableExpression|DirectlyAssignableExpression)//T-Identifier[ let $name := @Text return (: local var/val declared (or inferred) as String in the enclosing function, if any (may shadow a class property of the same name) :) let $local := ancestor::FunctionBody//PropertyDeclaration[VariableDeclaration/@Identifier = $name][1] return if ($local) then $local[pmd-kotlin:typeIs('kotlin.String')] else (: no local shadow: look up a class/object-level String property; also covers use inside scope functions like apply/run/let :) (ancestor::ClassDeclaration|ancestor::ObjectDeclaration)[1]/ClassBody/ClassMemberDeclarations/ClassMemberDeclaration/Declaration/PropertyDeclaration [VariableDeclaration/@Identifier = $name] [pmd-kotlin:typeIs('kotlin.String')] ]/@Text (: only a violation if some SINGLE name occurs 2+ times, not 2+ different vars each concatenated once :) return some $n in distinct-values($qualifyingNames) satisfies count($qualifyingNames[. = $n]) > 1 ] //Statement[Assignment//(T-ADD_ASSIGNMENT|T-ADD)][position()=last()]

rule.name: AvoidCalendar
rule.message: A Calendar is inefficient in memory usage.
rule.description: Problem: A Calendar is a heavyweight object and expensive to create. Solution: Use java.time.LocalDateTime or java.time.ZonedDateTime instead. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCalendarDateCreation
rule.message: A Calendar is used to get a Date or millis; this is expensive. Use LocalDate.now(), Instant.now() or System.currentTimeMillis().
rule.description: Problem: Calendar.getInstance() is expensive as it scans locale and timezone configuration. Using it just to get the current time or a Date object wastes CPU. Solution: Use java.time.LocalDate.now(), java.time.Instant.now() or System.currentTimeMillis() for timestamps. (jpinpoint-rules)
rule.example: import java.util.Calendar fun bad() = Calendar.getInstance().getTime() // bad: expensive fun good() = java.time.Instant.now() // ok: idiomatic Kotlin/Java fun goodMs() = System.currentTimeMillis() // ok

rule.name: AvoidLoadingAllFromFile
rule.message: Files.readAll methods and similar APIs load all bytes into memory: a risk of memory problems.
rule.description: Problem: APIs like Files.readAllBytes, Files.readAllLines, Files.readString, InputStream.readAllBytes, IOUtils.toByteArray, ByteArrayOutputStream.toByteArray load entire content into heap memory. This risks OutOfMemoryError, long GC pauses, and slow responses when processing large files. Solution: Use streaming APIs end-to-end, do not buffer whole files in memory. Note: Not a problem for small files. Use @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidLoadingAllFromFile") then. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath
property.value: //PostfixUnaryExpression[ pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('java.nio.file.Files#readAllBytes(*)') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('java.nio.file.Files#readAllLines(*)') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('java.nio.file.Files#readString(*)') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('java.io.InputStream#readAllBytes()') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream#toByteArray()') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('org.springframework.util.ResizableByteArrayOutputStream#toByteArray()') or pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils#toByteArray(*)') ]

rule.example:
import java.nio.file.Files import java.nio.file.Path
fun bad(path: Path): ByteArray = Files.readAllBytes(path) // bad fun good(path: Path) = Files.newInputStream(path).use { it.copyTo(System.out) } // good
